prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: natural-history reconstruction of the invented dinosaur Digosaurus, isolated transparent PNG for a cartoon-versus-real-animal comparison.
USER'S CORRECTED GOAL: Imagine that input image 1 is a highly simplified children's cartoon OF an actual prehistoric animal. Reconstruct the real dinosaur that inspired that cartoon. REDESIGN THE ANATOMY from the skeleton outward. The primary objective is realistic dinosaur morphology, not covering the cartoon's anatomy in realistic skin.
Reference roles: Image 1 = identity and broad colour-pattern clues only. Image 2 = realistic prehistoric flight anatomy/material reference. Image 3 = realistic theropod skull, pelvis, posture, feet and tail reference. Neither reference 2 nor 3 should appear as an additional animal.
Subject and skeletal design: A single believable, adult small-to-medium theropod-like dinosaur specialized for digging and flight. Clear elongated dinosaur skull and tapering reptilian snout, nostrils near the snout tip, small laterally placed amber eyes in proper bony sockets, closed straight natural jaw with no facial expression. Anatomical S-curved neck leading into a muscular, horizontally carried ribcage, substantial flight musculature across the chest and shoulder girdle, narrow animal pelvis, muscular hind thighs, correctly articulated digitigrade lower legs with raised heels and broad weight-bearing three-toed feet bearing stout curved digging claws. A long tapering balancing tail emerges naturally behind the pelvis. Exactly four limbs: two hind legs and two forelimbs modified into large membranous wings, no extra arms or extra legs. Wing shoulders, upper arm, elbow, forearm and elongated supporting digits are visibly coherent, with tensioned skin membranes joining the forelimbs to the flanks. Featherless wing membranes like a plausible speculative small scansoriopterygid-style dinosaur reconstruction, not decorative bat wings stuck onto its back. Wings partly extended in a natural alert stance, forelimb free claws capable of raking soil as well. The resulting silhouette must look like a real prehistoric animal in a museum-quality reconstruction.
Translate the cartoon identity biologically: tall red head triangle becomes a thin low-to-moderate bony cranial crest swept backwards; side points become two short cranial ridges, the pink side frills become a subtle short nape display fringe. Body muted dusty rose with mottled earthy red on the head and wing leading edges. The wings retain naturally mottled dark-brown, olive/lime-green and blue-green/turquoise bands, with subdued plausible animal pigmentation. Hind legs have slate-cobalt blue pigmentation, feet horn-coloured. Cream underside with a faint irregular vaguely heart-shaped light patch ONLY; REMOVE the drawn dinosaur-head logo entirely because a real animal has no printed emblem. Replace face-shaped cream mask with ordinary lighter jaw and throat countershading.
Rendering: Extremely convincing natural-history paleoart with lifelike animal proportions, photographic realism, nonuniform fine scales, subtle short filamentous covering on parts of torso and nape, tendon definition, skin folds, keratin claw wear, fine wrinkles and visible structural fibres in wing membranes. Natural soft daylight and restrained highlights. Three-quarter SIDE VIEW with head to the left, torso and long tail visible, standing with one digging foot beside a very small disturbed soil mound. Full body, all wing tips, entire tail and feet within the frame, comfortable margins. Wide landscape framing as needed for the real animal's long body and wings.
Transparent alpha background; no environment or backdrop. No labels, text, watermark.
CRITICAL NEGATIVES: no cartoon oval upright torso, no round human-like face, no smile or wink, no eyelashes, no giant eyes, no baby proportions, no humanoid posture, no hanging human-shaped blue legs, no pink hairstyle, no heart badge or dinosaur emblem, no toy, no cute mascot, no dragon horns, no six-limbed dragon. Prioritize plausible prehistoric anatomy over literal cartoon shapes.
